BotTracking.AIAssistantsReportDocumentation: Discover which AI assistants are crawling your site and how many hits each one generates. Expand a bot to review the most frequently requested pages or documents.
BotTracking.AIAssistantsOverviewHelp1: The AI Assistant Overview page provide insights into website traffic originating from AI Assistants such as ChatGPT and other large language model–based assistants. These reports track key metrics including the number of requests made by these bots, the pages and documents they access, and any errors encountered. They also offer detailed breakdowns showing which bots visit specific page URLs, helping you understand how AI assistants interact with your content and identify opportunities to improve visibility and accessibility for AI-driven users.
BotTracking.AIAssistantsOverviewHelp2: It’s important to note that none of these pages were actually viewed by humans in the traditional way — all requests originate from AI assistants fetching content automatically.
BotTracking.AIAssistantsOverviewHelp3: Currently, these reports exclusively include requests from AI bots that do not execute JavaScript. They do not include traffic from AI crawlers used for training AI models or from AI agents capable of executing JavaScript.
BotTracking.ColumnAcquiredVisitsDocumentation: Visits that started after someone clicked from an AI assistant (Referrers → AI Assistants).
BotTracking.ColumnDocumentRequestsDocumentation: Total number of bot requests to document URLs recorded during the selected period.
BotTracking.ColumnPageRequestsDocumentation: Total number of bot requests to page URLs recorded during the selected period.
BotTracking.ColumnRequestsDocumentation: Total number of bot requests recorded during the selected period. Includes both page and document URLs.
BotTracking.ColumnUniquePageUrlsDocumentation: Distinct page URLs requested by AI assistants.
BotTracking.ColumnUniqueDocumentUrlsDocumentation: Distinct download or document URLs requested by AI assistants.
BotTracking.ColumnUniqueAiChatbotsDocumentation: AI assistant user agents detected during the selected period.
BotTracking.ColumnNotFoundRequestsDocumentation: Number of bot requests that returned an HTTP 404 or 410 response, including document URLs.
BotTracking.ColumnServerErrorRequestsDocumentation: Number of bot requests that returned an HTTP 5xx response, including document URLs.
BotTracking.ColumnClickThroughRateDocumentation: Share of AI assistant requests that resulted in acquired visits (acquired visits ÷ requests).
BotTracking.BotsOverTimeReportDocumentation: This report charts the evolution of AI assistant activity. Click any metric to enlarge its graph and review the underlying trend.
BotTracking.PluginDescription: Track and analyze visits from AI bots such as ChatGPT-User and similar. This plugin helps you understand how AI-driven tools interact with your website by logging and reporting bot-triggered requests.
BotTracking.SegmentNotSupported: Report does not support segmentation. The data displayed is your standard, unsegmented report data.
BotTracking.NoDataCloudflareInstructions1: This integration uses a Cloudflare Worker that proxies requests to your origin and asynchronously posts Matomo hits without delaying responses. The tracker code is maintained externally, so follow the repository README for the current setup and deployment details.
BotTracking.NoDataCloudflareInstructions2: Deploy the Worker (Node.js) and set your Matomo URL and site ID.
BotTracking.NoDataCloudflareInstructions3: Attach the Worker to your zone or route so it runs inline with requests.
BotTracking.NoDataCloudflareInstructions4: Verify the setup by checking that AI Chatbot hits are showing in tracking reports.
BotTracking.NoDataCloudFrontInstructions1: This integration uses an AWS Lambda that reads CloudFront access logs from S3 and sends Matomo hits in batches. The tracker code is maintained externally, so follow the repository README for the current setup and deployment details.
BotTracking.NoDataCloudFrontInstructions2: Deploy the Lambda (Node.js) and set your Matomo URL and site ID.
BotTracking.NoDataCloudFrontInstructions3: Attach an S3 trigger for CloudFront log objects (for example, ObjectCreated on .gz logs).
BotTracking.NoDataCloudFrontInstructions4: Verify the setup by checking that AI Chatbot hits are showing in tracking reports.
BotTracking.NoDataWordPressInstructions1: The WordPress integration adds a small bridge that sends AI Chatbot signals to Matomo. Because the tracker is maintained externally, the README is the source of truth for current steps.
BotTracking.NoDataWordPressInstructions3: Enter your Matomo URL and site ID.
BotTracking.NoDataWordPressInstructions4: Verify the setup by checking that AI Chatbot hits are showing in tracking reports.
